title: Fit Body, Fit Mind, Fit Nation

learn.hook: Can you stand like a mountain and balance like a tree? Yoga lets you try!
points: The lesson 'Fit Body, Fit Mind, Fit Nation' says that fit, healthy people make a strong country.
Being fit means having a strong, healthy body and a calm, happy mind.
Running, skipping, cycling, swimming and outdoor games keep us fit.
Yoga is an old Indian practice of body poses (asanas), slow breathing and relaxing.
International Day of Yoga is celebrated every year on 21 June.

example.q: Read: Every morning, Anaya and her grandfather do yoga on the terrace in Pune. First they stand tall like a mountain in Tadasana. Then they balance on one leg like a tree in Vrikshasana. They breathe in slowly and breathe out slowly. "Now my body feels strong and my mind feels calm," says Anaya. Question: How does yoga help Anaya?
steps: Find what Anaya says at the end.
'Now my body feels strong and my mind feels calm.'
So yoga helps both her body and her mind.
example.answer: It makes her body feel strong and her mind feel calm.

learn.reallife: Try stretching for a few minutes every morning with a grown-up. Learn new poses only from a teacher or an adult who knows yoga.

games.title: Fitness: true or false?
items: Breathing slowly is an important part of yoga.
International Day of Yoga is on 21 June.
It is celebrated every year on 21 June.
Being fit is only about the body, not the mind.
A fit person has a healthy body and a calm mind.
It is safest to learn new yoga poses with a teacher or an adult.
A teacher shows the right way so you do not get hurt.
Children need to play and move every day too.

quiz.q: Story line: "Anaya and her grandfather do yoga on the terrace in Pune." Where do they do yoga?
quiz.explain: The story says they do yoga on the terrace.
quiz.mistake: Does not find the place word

quiz.q: Story line: "First they stand tall like a mountain in Tadasana." Tadasana is called the ___ pose.
quiz.explain: In Tadasana you stand tall and still like a mountain.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of yoga poses

quiz.q: Which pose needs you to balance on one leg like a tree?
quiz.explain: In Vrikshasana, the tree pose, you balance on one leg.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of yoga poses

quiz.q: On which date is International Day of Yoga celebrated?
quiz.explain: International Day of Yoga is on 21 June every year.
quiz.mistake: Mixes it up with other special days

quiz.q: Anaya says, "Now my body feels strong and my mind feels calm." How does she feel after yoga?
quiz.explain: She says her body feels strong and her mind feels calm.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the words she says as a clue

quiz.q: Which of these keeps a child fit?
quiz.explain: Skipping makes the body move and keeps it strong.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which activities are exercise

quiz.q: Bhujangasana is named after which animal?
quiz.explain: Bhujangasana is the cobra pose. You lift your chest like a cobra raising its head.
quiz.mistake: Guesses an animal without knowing the pose

quiz.q: In 'Fit Nation', what does 'nation' mean?
quiz.explain: A nation is a country and all the people who live in it.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'nation'

teach.ask: Gappu wants to be fit. What does being fit mean, and how can yoga help Gappu?
teach.praise: Yes! A fit body is strong and a fit mind is calm. Yoga poses and slow breathing help both. Gappu is trying the tree pose!
teach.nudge: What happens to the body and the mind when we are fit? What do we do in yoga?

learn.hook: A habit is something you do again and again. Is your habit helpful or harmful?
points: Healthy habits: eat fruits and vegetables, drink clean water, sleep on time and play outdoors.
Wash your hands with soap before eating, and brush your teeth twice a day.
Too much junk food and screen time are not good for us.
The suffix '-ful' means 'full of': help + ful = helpful, care + ful = careful.
The suffix '-less' means 'without': care + less = careless, harm + less = harmless.

example.q: Think it through: 'Eating only junk food every day can be ___ for your body.' Is it 'harmful' or 'harmless'?
steps: 'Harmful' means full of harm. 'Harmless' means without harm.
Too much junk food is bad for the body.

learn.reallife: Make a habit chart at home. Tick it each day you drink enough water, play outside and sleep on time.

games.title: Healthy or unhealthy?
items: Watching screens till late at night

items.text: Cross the road in a care___ way.
A pencil with no lead is use___.
Thank you for being so help___!
This little spider is harm___. It will not hurt you.

quiz.q: Which of these is a healthy habit?
quiz.explain: Washing hands removes germs before we eat.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which habits keep us healthy

quiz.q: How often should we brush our teeth?
quiz.explain: We should brush our teeth twice a day, in the morning and at night.
quiz.mistake: Thinks brushing is needed only sometimes

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'careful'?
quiz.explain: -ful means 'full of' and -less means 'without'. Careful and careless are opposites.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what -less means

quiz.q: What does 'helpful' mean?
quiz.explain: Help + ful means full of help, so a helpful person is ready to help.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up -ful and -less

quiz.q: What does 'harmless' mean?
quiz.explain: -less means 'without', so harmless means without harm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks -less means 'more'

quiz.q: Choose the correct spelling: "Drinking clean water is ___ for our health."
quiz.explain: The suffix is spelt '-ful' with one l: useful.
quiz.mistake: Spells the suffix with two l's

quiz.q: Which is the healthiest snack?
quiz.explain: Fruits like bananas give us energy and goodness.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tasty but unhealthy snack

quiz.q: Why should we wash our hands with soap?
quiz.explain: Soap and water wash away germs that can make us ill.
quiz.mistake: Does not know why soap is used

teach.ask: Gappu eats sweets all day, sleeps late and never washes his wings. What healthy habits can you teach Gappu?
teach.praise: Great advice! Wash with soap, eat fruits and vegetables, sleep on time and play outside. Gappu feels so fresh!
teach.nudge: What should Gappu eat? And what should Gappu do before eating and at night?

learn.hook: Do you breathe quickly or slowly in yoga? The answer is an adverb!
points: An adverb tells us more about a verb (an action word).
Some adverbs tell HOW: slowly, quickly, gently, loudly, carefully.
Some adverbs tell WHEN: today, now, early, tomorrow. Some tell WHERE: outside, here, there.
Many 'how' adverbs are made by adding -ly to an adjective: slow → slowly, quick → quickly.
If the word ends in y, change y to i: happy → happily, easy → easily.

example.q: Think it through: find the adverb in 'Anaya breathes slowly.'
steps: Ask: how does she breathe? Slowly.
'Slowly' tells us more about the verb, so it is an adverb.

learn.reallife: Your PE teacher says 'run quickly', 'stretch slowly' and 'land softly'. Those are adverbs!

quiz.q: Find the adverb: "Anaya stretches slowly."
quiz.explain: 'Slowly' tells how Anaya stretches.
quiz.mistake: Picks the verb instead of the word that tells how

quiz.q: Fill in: "The cheetah runs ___."
quiz.explain: We need a word that tells how it runs: quickly.
quiz.mistake: Uses an adjective where an adverb is needed

quiz.q: Which word tells HOW in "Grandpa lifts the baby gently"?
quiz.explain: 'Gently' tells how Grandpa lifts the baby.
quiz.mistake: Picks the verb or a noun

quiz.q: Which is the correct adverb made from 'happy'?
quiz.explain: Change y to i and add -ly: happily.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change y to i

quiz.q: Fill in: "Please speak ___ in the library."
quiz.explain: We speak softly in a library so others can read.
quiz.mistake: Uses a noun where an adverb is needed

quiz.q: Which of these words is an adverb?
quiz.explain: 'Carefully' tells how an action is done.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up adjectives and adverbs

quiz.q: Which word tells WHEN in "We will go to the park tomorrow"?
quiz.explain: 'Tomorrow' tells when we will go.
quiz.mistake: Picks a place word instead of a time word

quiz.q: Which word tells WHERE in "The children are playing outside"?
quiz.explain: 'Outside' tells where the children are playing.
quiz.mistake: Picks the verb instead of the place word

teach.ask: Gappu says 'I fly quick.' A friend says it should be 'I fly quickly.' Why? What is an adverb?
teach.praise: Super! An adverb tells more about a verb, like how it is done. 'Quickly' tells how Gappu flies. Zoom, Gappu!
teach.nudge: What does an adverb tell us about the action? What do we often add at the end of 'quick'?
